## 固定收益開場論點

7月30日，美國公債延續聯準會會後的殖利率曲線趨陡走勢，但幅度遠小於會後首波重新定價；當時主席Kevin Warsh未升息，也未向投資人提出明確的反應函數。2年期殖利率下跌2.7個基點至4.247%，5年期下降2.1個基點至4.388%，10年期微降0.5個基點至4.674%，30年期則上升1.2個基點至5.215%。2年與10年期利差擴大2.2個基點至42.7個基點，2年與30年期利差擴大3.9個基點至96.8個基點。

長端殖利率盤中一度升至更極端的水準。30年期觸及約5.24%，續創19年新高，10年期也逼近4.69%。截至最新收盤，30年期殖利率一個月來已上升35個基點，高於10年期的29.8個基點與2年期的14個基點。投資人不再只是剔除聯準會立即升息的風險；當央行仰賴市場殖利率抑制經濟，卻未說明通膨若持續偏高將如何調整政策，市場也開始要求更高的風險補償。

週四公布的數據使這項矛盾更加鮮明，而非得到化解。美國第2季經濟成長年率放緩至1.5%，但消費支出成長3.2%，企業投資仍強，私人國內需求更創2023年初以來最快增速。6月通膨較為溫和，個人消費支出物價指數較5月下跌0.1%，年增率由4.1%降至3.7%；然而，這一增速仍遠高於聯準會2%的目標，中東戰事重啟也使單月能源成本下降不足以構成持久的通膨訊號。

美債殖利率的組成顯示，市場在會後劇烈調整後已有所穩定。週四10年期實質殖利率上升0.5個基點至2.414%，10年期損益兩平通膨率則下降1個基點至2.26%，兩者共同造成名目殖利率小幅下滑，與聯準會決策後長天期通膨補償急升的情況形成對比。最初反應中，30年期損益兩平通膨率曾上升6個基點至2.23%，為2024年11月以來最大漲幅，反映投資人質疑Warsh對既有通膨框架的承諾。

跨資產收盤表現進一步凸顯短暫釋壓與持續長天期壓力之間的差異。科技股反彈帶動標普500指數上漲1.66%、那斯達克100指數上漲3.36%，費城半導體指數更大漲8.19%，但半導體指數一個月來仍下跌17.55%。美元指數下跌0.73%，黃金期貨上漲3.29%。長天期美債既未充分參與風險資產的反彈，也未明顯受惠於油價下跌，殖利率曲線遠端仍由通膨與期限溢價之爭主導。

## 需求展現韌性，聯準會反應函數仍未明朗

1.5%的GDP整體增速低估了國內需求的強度。約占經濟三分之二的消費支出以3.2%的年率加速成長；剔除庫存、淨出口與政府支出的國內私人購買者最終銷售成長3.9%，不僅超過第1季增速的兩倍，也是2023年初以來最強表現。

企業投資成長8.4%，動能來自人工智慧基礎設施持續擴建，以及工業與運輸設備支出。工業設備投資創2011年以來最大增幅，運輸設備支出則出現兩年來最大成長；資訊處理設備與軟體也強勁擴張，只是速度稍慢。

整體經濟增速較弱，主要是淨出口扣除1個百分點、庫存再拖累0.67個百分點。進口偏高，部分原因是企業趕在新一輪關稅上路前將商品運入美國；伊朗衝突期間，企業也持續消化庫存。住宅投資則自2024年底以來首次對成長帶來小幅正貢獻。

家庭需求延續至6月。經通膨調整的消費支出成長0.4%，追平2025年7月以來最大增幅，耐久財、休閒、餐飲與住宿支出均提供支撐。不過，儲蓄率已降至2022年以來最低，7月汽油價格再度上漲，也可能侵蝕先前退稅與促銷活動帶來的支持。

通膨數據較為有利，卻未消除政策矛盾。6月PCE物價指數下跌0.1%，年增率由5月的4.1%降至符合經濟學家預期的3.7%；排除食品與能源的指標增幅也低於預期。但這項改善發生在美國與伊朗一度停火、能源成本下降的月份，戰事重啟後能否持續仍有疑問。

每週初領失業救濟金人數維持低檔，也從另一面顯示勞動市場尚未弱到足以迫使聯準會偏離通膨目標。單月物價轉弱、就業穩健，加上私人國內需求成長3.9%，既提供耐心等待的理由，也支持最終收緊政策，卻未見通膨或經濟活動明確惡化到足以確立下次行動時點。

利率市場在排除7月立即行動的風險後，因而重新納入部分9月升息機率。交換市場顯示，9月會議升息25個基點的機率約為三分之二，低於聯準會決定將利率維持在3.5%至3.75%前市場幾乎完全反映的水準；年底前第二次升息的隱含機率則降至約40%。

7月決策塵埃落定，也引發大規模部位平倉。8月聯邦基金期貨未平倉量減少約14萬口；此前部位曾超過100萬口，名目曝險約$5兆。這項合約在9月會議前到期，原已成為避險立即升息風險的主要工具。利率維持不變後，合約價格迅速上漲，迫使空頭回補或減碼。

這項調整可以解釋前端殖利率下降，卻不足以說明長端為何持續承壓。Warsh強調，較高的市場殖利率已在抑制經濟，可以代替央行完成部分緊縮工作。若聯準會因市場借款成本偏高而維持利率不變，在通膨回歸目標獲得更明確證據以前，投資人便沒有充分理由主動壓低這些成本。市場主導的緊縮因此具有自我強化特性：長端殖利率若下降，就會削弱央行用來延後升息的部分緊縮力量。

Warsh表示正在研究比PCE更廣泛的一組通膨指標，又增添一項不確定性。他仍承諾將通膨降至2%，並表示聯準會目前仍使用PCE；但他並未提出替代指標，也未排除檢討政策框架與經濟數據的工作小組在1月後影響策略的可能性。

指標選擇會改變投資人對通膨目標及其達成路徑的理解，因此這種模糊性相當重要。前里奇蒙聯準銀行總裁Jeffrey Lacker認為，PCE與消費者物價指數是僅有的兩項廣泛且可靠的選擇。摩根大通經濟學家Michael Feroli警告，改變框架可能被視為重新定義通膨問題，而非解決問題；巴克萊策略師Jon Hill則認為，市場對聯準會承諾的信心下降，將推高期限溢價與通膨風險溢價。

週四10年期損益兩平通膨率下降1個基點，顯示這項疑慮並未在整個交易時段持續加劇。不過，最初的會後漲勢集中在殖利率曲線更遠端，而政策框架改變在這些年期的累積影響最大，因此風險仍不容忽視。現券交易活動增幅最大的也是30年期區段：20年以上美債的面額成交量較週三增加17.8%，10年以上至20年期區段增加37.5%。這些數字指出重新定價的重心，卻無法判斷客戶是淨買方或淨賣方。

中東情勢使通膨可能結果的分布維持寬廣。德黑蘭攻擊美國位於約旦的基地後，美國空襲數十處伊朗軍事目標。無人機也擊中埃及地中海沿岸附近的兩艘液化天然氣運輸船，沙烏地阿拉伯與伊拉克則更直接地捲入日益擴大的衝突。

儘管如此，油價仍然下跌，原因是美國的攻擊避開關鍵橋梁與其他民用基礎設施，荷莫茲海峽航運也出現復甦跡象。卡達在逾三週後首度讓一批LNG貨物通過海峽。布蘭特原油下跌1.5%至$89.38，WTI下跌0.56%至$83.99，但一個月來仍分別上漲22.19%與18.71%。單日油價下跌抑制了損益兩平通膨率，但累計漲幅與持續發生的攻擊，意味能源衝擊尚未成為過去式。

## 英國央行紓解英債壓力，日本出手捍衛日圓

英國央行將當前國內通膨降溫與能源所帶來的條件式威脅分開看待，因而促成更明顯的前端英債反彈。貨幣政策委員會以6比3決議將銀行利率維持在3.75%。Catherine Mann與Megan Greene及首席經濟學家Huw Pill一同支持升息25個基點，但總裁Andrew Bailey與其餘5名委員認為，國內物價壓力已充分緩和，可以繼續觀望。

Bailey明確否認委員會正逐步接近升息。通常被視為立場較鷹派的副總裁Clare Lombardelli也表示，維持利率不變並不是一個難以抉擇的決定。決策官員指出，國內通膨壓力已有明顯轉弱跡象，能源成本上升也幾乎尚未擴散至工資及更廣泛的物價。

交易員將9月升息機率下調至約35%，並反映年底前約32個基點的緊縮幅度，低於週三的42個基點。2年期英債殖利率大跌11個基點至4.34%，為6月12日以來最大降幅；10年期下降4個基點至4.99%，30年期則大致持平於5.73%。殖利率曲線因而像美國一樣趨陡，但英國的動力來自央行更直接地抗拒近期升息。

表決結果凸顯官員對如何處理能源衝擊的分歧日益擴大。Pill主張升息可以排除商品市場雜訊，Mann強調政策可信度，Greene則認為提早行動可降低第二輪效應的機率。另一方的副總裁Dave Ramsden與外部委員Alan Taylor表示，如果衝突迅速結束、國內通膨持續降溫，可以考慮恢復降息。

英國央行的基準預測顯示，通膨率將由目前的2.6%升至2026年底的3.2%，明年再朝2%回落；這項路徑假設中東衝突持續呈現時斷時續的狀態。在油價高於$100、天然氣價格上漲60%的不利情境下，通膨率會在2027年第2季升至4.5%；若情勢較溫和、衝突更快降溫，通膨高點則為3%，第二輪效應也較小。各種情境下，2026年與2027年的GDP成長率均維持在約1%。

資產負債表政策使英債曲線較遠端持續承壓。英國央行估計，量化緊縮已使10年期殖利率上升20至30個基點，比一年前的估計高約5個基點，並將於9月決定下一年度的計畫。秋季預算公布前的財政不確定性，也使長天期投資人更缺乏追隨前端反彈的理由。

歐元區數據則從另一個角度顯示，放鬆金融情勢仍需謹慎。第2季GDP成長0.4%，扭轉年初停滯，不僅是市場共識預測的兩倍，也是逾一年來最強的單季增幅。儘管伊朗戰爭推高能源成本，四大經濟體仍全數擴張。

德國成長0.2%，第1季增幅則上修至0.4%。法國在前季萎縮0.1%後成長0.2%，消費支出與貿易抵銷投資連續第二季下降的影響；義大利同樣成長0.2%。西班牙再度以0.7%的增幅領先，獲得家庭支出、觀光、移民與歐盟基金支持。

經濟成長優於預期之際，通膨訊號也轉強。西班牙7月通膨率加速至3.8%，德國地區性數據同樣上升，週五公布的歐元區通膨率預料將微升至2.9%。歐洲央行先前已警告，能源衝擊同時帶來通膨上行與成長下行風險；較強的產出數據削弱了其中的成長下行證據，也支持9月可能再度升息的預期。

日本面臨貨幣政策、主權債殖利率與匯率更直接的衝突。據市場人士及《日本經濟新聞》報導，日本當局進場支撐日圓後，日圓在紐約交易時段兌美元一度升值3.3%，創2023年12月以來最大盤中漲幅。美國當局也要求市場提供美元兌日圓報價，這通常是評估市場狀況的步驟。美國財政部長Scott Bessent表示，日圓遭到嚴重低估，過度波動並不健康。

日圓收在每美元159.53日圓，亞洲早盤仍保有大部分升幅。這波走勢延續美元在聯準會會後的廣泛跌勢，又正值日本央行決策前夕，使市場更可能將干預與貨幣政策指引一併評估。日本前一季已動用創紀錄的¥11.73兆支撐日圓，其中部分資金可能取自包括美債在內的外國證券部位。

日本國內債市也顯示進一步正常化的壓力。2年期JGB標售的投標倍數為3.63，低於前次的4.82及12個月平均3.81；即使該券提供今年以來最高殖利率，標售尾差仍由0.005擴大至0.007。2年期殖利率約為1.47%，接近7月稍早觸及的1.52%高點。

這次標售並非失敗，但今年最高殖利率仍未使需求回到近期平均水準。隔夜指數交換市場顯示，日本央行9月前升息的機率約為25%，10月前則為79%。雖然市場仍預期本次會議將維持利率不變，但標售需求轉弱、官方再次干預，以及日圓對美日利差的敏感度，都提高了總裁植田和男政策指引的重要性。

## AI借款人讓步於定價與保障條款後完成融資

人工智慧融資的重新定價已從協商進入完成交易階段。CoreWeave敲定一筆$26億槓桿貸款，利差為基準利率加550個基點，比最初425至450個基點區間的上限高100個基點。貸款發行價為每美元96至97美分，預期殖利率超過9%。

這些讓步吸引約$90億訂單，使交易得以完成；但以最初行銷利差區間上限計算，估計每年將多付約$3,000萬利息。CoreWeave一檔歐元公司債的利差在週四交易期間一度觸及1,000個基點；部分公司債近期也曾跌破每美元90美分、殖利率升至10%區間低端，之後才隨科技股大盤反彈而回升。

這筆貸款用於採購晶片及其他運算設備，以履行涉及Anthropic、Jane Street與Hudson River Trading的照付不議合約。貸款可分期動用，因此只需就實際借款金額付息，本金並會在存續期內攤還至零。穆迪給予Ba2評等，惠譽評為BB+，均位於投機級較高端。

這項結構仍未消除最主要的期限錯配。相關客戶合約的加權平均年限約3.1年，短於貸款的5年期限；客戶協議最初簽約收入約為$40億，CoreWeave並承諾在找到替代租戶前補足現金流缺口。即便如此，貸款人仍須承擔續約與剩餘需求風險，其程度高於CoreWeave先前由晶片擔保、廣泛聯貸的融資。

這項差異解釋了為何$90億訂單可與大幅提高的定價並存。投資人願意為可辨識的合約與擔保品提供資金，但租約可能早於債務到期，因此要求額外補償。交易進行之際，CoreWeave正準備今年支出逾$340億，市場上接連出現的資料中心交易也在爭奪同一批資金。

Proofpoint的$50億再融資同樣要在貸款人改變交易條件後才得以完成。這家由Thoma Bravo持有的資安公司將$43億貸款期限延長兩年，另有$7.35億仍於2028年到期。延期部分的定價為基準利率加450個基點，高於現有融資的300個基點。

公司調整了約24項條款。其中，全方位阻斷條款限制可能把擔保品移出現有貸款人權利範圍的交易，另一項條款則禁止偏袒特定債權人的私下協商債務回購。訂單原本已足以在初始期限前通過交易，但部分投資人是基於將加入這些保障條款的預期才提交承諾，促使交易流程延期。

CoreWeave與Proofpoint因此透過同一股債權人權力增強的趨勢，完成兩種不同的科技融資。CoreWeave為有合約支持的成長資金支付更高成本，但相關租約早於債務到期；Proofpoint為受到AI衝擊的成熟軟體業資本結構辦理再融資，不僅提高利差，也放棄部分契約彈性。交易完成證明兩家公司仍可取得資本，定價與保障條款則揭示取得資金所附帶的條件。

投資級借款人也面臨相同的資金供給限制，只是利差較低。Equinix開始行銷至少$30億債券，最多分為4個券次，期限由3年至10年；最長券次的初步定價指引約為美債加140個基點。這家資料中心公司第2季資本支出較一年前增加60%，達$15.8億，募集資金擬用於收購不動產與企業、開發計畫及償還債務。

這筆交易使市場在已持續吸收貸款、專案債與公司債發行之際，又迎來一宗大型AI相關融資。Equinix與CoreWeave不同，具有投資級市場准入資格與多元化的資料中心組合；但其公布的規模與資金用途，仍使最終定價成為重要觀察指標，可用來判斷融資成本上升究竟仍集中在高槓桿借款人，或已擴散至基礎設施產業。

銀行也在移轉部分基礎設施擴建曝險。法國興業銀行接近完成一筆重大風險移轉交易，涵蓋約$50億能源、再生電力及資料中心專案融資貸款。這類交易通常為參照投資組合的5%至15%提供保障，讓銀行釋放監理資本，投資人則可取得有時超過10%的票息。

2026年上半年SRT發行額超過$180億，高於一年前的約$150億，並有望連續第六年創下年度紀錄。法國興業銀行近期也在另一筆交易中移轉逾€90億公司貸款風險，定價為基準利率加675個基點。市場持續成長，顯示銀行可繼續承作基礎設施貸款，同時將集中的第一損失曝險分配給專業投資人。

需求也在轉向較短天期的公司債。過去一個月，5年內到期的債券表現優於整體歐元投資級指數，美國信用債也呈現類似格局。1年內到期的債券同期大致持平，整體指數則下跌0.9%，10年以上到期債券更下跌逾2.9%。由3年期延長至9年期，殖利率僅增加67個基點，對承擔大幅增加的利率曝險補償有限。

這種偏好與美債殖利率曲線及初級市場讓利一致。投資人可在短至中期債券保留利息收益，而不必完整承受期限溢價上升的影響。較長天期公司債則同時暴露於美債利率風險，以及大量科技業發債可能要求額外信用利差的風險。

## 私人信貸違約攀升，長天期美元融資更為困難

私人信貸的壓力已發展得更為明顯。惠譽評等追蹤的1,300家美國私人債務借款人，其過去12個月違約率在第2季末升至創紀錄的6%，高於第1季原先高點5.7%。該季32起違約事件涉及20家新出現的違約借款人，使違約借款人總數增至84家。

受壓力所迫的到期日展延，已超越以債付息（PIK）安排與延後付息，成為該季最主要的違約來源。32起事件中超過半數涉及展延，顯示即使貸款人避免傳統意義上的付款違約，愈來愈多借款人仍無法按原定時程完成再融資。

工業與製造業的產業違約率最高，由第1季的5.9%升至10.4%；醫療業則由6.9%升至9.4%。軟體業走勢相反，違約率由2.3%降至1.2%，儘管投資人仍擔心AI削弱既有科技企業。惠譽預期違約率將持續偏高，因為降息尚未到來，併購活動也依然低迷。

Xerox展示了受壓借款人在債務到期前籌措流動性的一種方式。公司第2季認列$1.05億關稅退款應收款，隨後以$8,000萬現金將這項權利出售給第三方，並將相當一部分所得用於以低於面額的價格回購債務。

公司債務總額為$42億，其中包括2028年8月到期、交易價格約為每美元60美分的$5.56億無擔保票據。收購Lexmark後，營收較一年前成長22%至$19億，但按備考基礎計算則下降7%。Xerox將全年營收預測上調至$76億，管理層則把2028年、2029年與2030年的到期債務列為資產負債表面臨的核心挑戰。

這項交易以較認列價值折讓24%的價格，將法律上仍具或有性的退款請求權換成即時現金。Xerox也因此得以折價清償債務，可能取得退款請求權現金售價與公司債務低迷市值之間的部分價差。交易提高了近期財務彈性，卻未改變仍須完成的再融資規模。

亞洲借款人的長天期美元融資同樣轉趨困難。投資人要求的殖利率高於印尼主權財富基金Danantara願意支付的水準，使其延後推進原訂20年期與30年期美元債券發行。長天期美債殖利率上升又放大了問題，因為規劃中的債券期限特別容易受基礎無風險殖利率曲線變動影響。

印尼央行總裁Perry Warjiyo辭職，也增加了發行人特有的風險溢價。據官員估計，Danantara控制的資產約值$9,000億，但成立僅略逾一年，市場持續質疑其治理、透明度，以及與總統Prabowo Subianto國家主導經濟計畫的關係。印尼盾今年以來兌美元貶值近8%；若交易成行，將是該基金繼6月首次發行$15億國際債券後的另一筆海外籌資。

其他新興市場借款人則尋求美元以外的選項。肯亞考慮在中國境內市場首次發行人民幣計價債券，可能在年底前籌措約相當於$3億的資金，用來支應截至2027年6月的財政赤字。今年發行的人民幣主權債與公司債平均殖利率約2.17%，不到新興市場美元債利率的一半。

相關計畫仍處初步階段，規模與時程都可能改變。肯亞預期財政赤字占GDP比率將由前一年的6.7%縮小至5.5%，但高額債務償付、政府積欠款項及稅收疲弱仍限制財政空間。其外債超過半數以美元計價，人民幣占比則為12%，因此熊貓債兼具降低融資成本與分散幣別的作用。

馬來西亞呈現亞洲本幣債券資金流動的另一面。外國投資人7月淨賣出$14億馬來西亞債券，為2024年10月以來最大流出。第2季GDP較一年前成長5.8%後，部分投資人將升息預期提前，使10年期殖利率當月上升約10個基點。

資金流出之際，馬來西亞通膨仍受控於1.9%，主權信用維持投資級，國內投資人基礎也曾使其債市在伊朗戰爭期間比數個區域同業更具韌性。多數受訪經濟學家預期，馬來西亞國家銀行至少到2027年都會將政策利率維持在2.75%。這種組合使市場容易受到短期外資調整部位影響，卻不足以證明該國財政或通膨基本面已持續惡化。

## 後市意義

日本央行7月31日決策是眼前的政策考驗。52名受訪經濟學家全數預期，在6月升息後，基準利率將維持在1%，市場焦點因此轉向更新後的預測、植田和男記者會及任何有關匯率的討論。若維持利率不變，同時保留10月升息的可能性，將符合目前交換市場定價；若訊息把緊縮推得更遠，捍衛日圓的重擔便會更多落在匯市干預上。

日本公債與政策的互動和利率決定同樣重要。2年期標售投標倍數僅3.63，尾差也擴大，顯示即使殖利率為今年最高，需求仍然轉弱。若央行提早釋出再次升息的指引，可能支撐日圓，卻也會進一步壓低短天期JGB價格；若延後更久，曾把日圓推至40年低點的利差交易可能再度活躍。

週五的歐元區通膨數據將決定，第2季成長優於預期是否伴隨更廣泛的物價加速。西班牙通膨已升至3.8%，德國地區性指標也加速；若歐元區數據接近預期的2.9%，9月升息仍會是歐洲央行的選項。若數據較弱，市場將更重視央行的另一項憂慮：能源衝擊可能先傷害成長，才形成持續的第二輪通膨。

對聯準會而言，接下來的通膨與就業數據不能只改變9月行動的機率，還必須釐清Warsh採用更廣泛通膨視角後，政策門檻是否改變。數據轉弱可能強化前端反彈；但若聯準會繼續把偏高的市場殖利率視為緊縮替代品，長端可能仍不易上漲。通膨若持續，7月的3名異議委員將顯得更具先見之明，也會增加央行採取行動、印證投資人已推動之殖利率曲線趨陡走勢的壓力。

美國財政部公布8月至10月季度標售規模，則構成另一項長天期利率風險考驗。市場預期規模維持不變，但投資人會評估融資指引是否在為明年擴大發行預作準備。30年期殖利率已高於5.2%；只要未來可能增加長天期借款的時點拉近，即使供給變動延後，也能影響期限溢價。

上述數據公布前，中東衝突仍可能改變各央行政策結果的分布。卡達恢復通行荷莫茲海峽，加上週四原油下跌，限制市場對美國新一輪空襲的即時通膨反應。若油輪、埃及水域或波斯灣基礎設施再遭攻擊，這項緩解將受到挑戰；若航運持續恢復，即使沒有全面政治和解，能源溢價仍可能下降。

評估AI融資時，交易能否以何種條件完成，比公布的認購需求更重要。CoreWeave雖吸引$90億訂單，卻是在敲定550個基點利差，並承擔客戶合約期限短於貸款所帶來的再融資風險後才完成交易。Proofpoint提高利差、加入債權人保障條款後，也成功延長大部分債務。Equinix的多券次債券發行，將顯示這波重新定價有多少會傳導至業務更多元、債券期限較短的投資級資料中心發行人。

最後必須區分資本是否仍可取得，以及資本是否仍然便宜。公司貸款、債券、SRT、熊貓債與受壓資產請求權出售，依然都是可用的融資來源；但條件已愈來愈多地反映美債殖利率曲線所呈現的共同壓力，包括偏高的實質殖利率、通膨不確定性、科技業龐大投資，以及市場對央行能否以明確指引穩定長期借款成本的信心下降。

overall_summary.headline: 聯準會不確定性持續壓抑長端，美債殖利率曲線趨陡
overall_summary.session_narrative:
截至7月30日收盤，2年期美債殖利率下跌2.7個基點至4.247%，10年期下降0.5個基點至4.674%，30年期則上升1.2個基點至5.215%。2年與30年期利差擴大3.9個基點至96.8個基點，30年期殖利率盤中更一度觸及約5.24%，創19年新高。這波走勢延續聯準會會後的曲線趨陡：7月維持利率不變，加上聯邦基金期貨大規模平倉，支撐美債前端；但在較長天期，投資人仍要求通膨風險與不明確反應函數的補償。

第2季GDP成長放緩至1.5%，但消費支出成長3.2%、私人國內需求成長3.9%，每週初領失業救濟金人數也維持低檔。6月PCE較前月下跌0.1%，年增率降至3.7%，但中東戰事重啟，使先前能源價格回落能否持續蒙上陰影。10年期實質殖利率上升0.5個基點，損益兩平通膨率下降1個基點，顯示最初的通膨風險重新定價只是趨於穩定，尚未完全逆轉。科技股大幅反彈、美元走弱與黃金上漲，也未能帶動長天期美債一同釋壓。

英國央行以6比3決議維持利率不變，帶動2年期英債殖利率下跌11個基點；日本干預日圓，加上2年期JGB標售需求轉弱，則提高了7月31日日本央行決策的重要性。科技業仍可取得融資，但條件更為嚴格：CoreWeave支付550個基點的利差，Proofpoint則提高融資成本並加入債權人保障條款。私人信貸違約率升至創紀錄的6%，受壓力所迫的到期日展延也成為最主要的違約形式。

## Opening Fixed-Income Thesis

Treasuries extended the post-Federal Reserve steepening on July 30, although the movement was far smaller than the initial repricing after Chair Kevin Warsh declined to raise rates or give investors a clear reaction function. The 2-year yield fell 2.7 basis points to 4.247%, the 5-year declined 2.1 basis points to 4.388% and the 10-year eased 0.5 basis point to 4.674%, while the 30-year rose 1.2 basis points to 5.215%. The 2s10s spread widened 2.2 basis points to 42.7 basis points and 2s30s increased 3.9 basis points to 96.8 basis points.

Long yields reached more extreme levels intraday. The 30-year touched about 5.24%, extending its rise to a fresh 19-year high, while the 10-year approached 4.69%. The latest close left the 30-year yield 35 basis points higher over a month, compared with increases of 29.8 basis points for the 10-year and 14 basis points for the 2-year. Investors were no longer merely removing the risk of an immediate Fed increase; they were charging more for the uncertainty created when the central bank relies on market yields to restrain the economy without specifying how policy will respond if inflation remains high.

Thursday’s data sharpened rather than resolved that problem. Second-quarter U.S. growth slowed to an annualized 1.5%, but consumer spending increased 3.2%, business investment remained strong and private domestic demand grew at its fastest pace since early 2023. June inflation was softer: the personal consumption expenditures price index fell 0.1% from May, while its annual rate eased to 3.7% from 4.1%. Yet that year-on-year pace remained far above the Fed’s 2% goal, and renewed fighting in the Middle East prevented one month of lower energy costs from providing a durable inflation signal.

The Treasury decomposition showed some stabilization after the violent post-meeting adjustment. The 10-year real yield rose 0.5 basis point to 2.414% on Thursday, while the 10-year breakeven rate declined 1 basis point to 2.26%. That combination accounted for the small decline in the nominal yield and contrasted with the surge in long-dated inflation compensation immediately after the Fed decision. The 30-year breakeven had increased 6 basis points to 2.23% in the initial reaction, its largest rise since November 2024, as investors questioned Warsh’s commitment to the established inflation framework.

The cross-asset close reinforced the distinction between short-lived relief and persistent duration pressure. The S&P 500 rose 1.66%, the Nasdaq 100 gained 3.36% and the Philadelphia Semiconductor Index jumped 8.19% as technology shares rebounded. The semiconductor gauge nevertheless remained 17.55% lower over a month. The dollar index fell 0.73%, while gold futures rose 3.29%. Long Treasuries failed to participate fully in the risk-asset recovery or benefit materially from lower oil, leaving the inflation and term-premium debate dominant at the far end of the curve.

## Resilient Demand Leaves the Fed’s Reaction Function Unsettled

The 1.5% GDP headline understated the strength of domestic demand. Consumer spending, which represents about two-thirds of the economy, accelerated at a 3.2% annualized rate. Final sales to private domestic purchasers, which exclude inventories, net exports and government spending, increased 3.9%, more than twice the first-quarter pace and the strongest result since early 2023.

Business investment grew at an 8.4% rate, supported by the continuing buildout of artificial-intelligence infrastructure as well as industrial and transportation equipment. Investment in industrial equipment recorded its largest increase since 2011, while transportation-equipment spending rose by the most in two years. Information-processing equipment and software also posted strong growth, albeit at a slower pace.

The weaker overall growth rate instead reflected a 1-percentage-point subtraction from net exports and a further 0.67-point drag from inventories. Imports were elevated partly because businesses brought goods into the country before another round of tariffs, while companies also drew down stocks during the Iran conflict. Residential investment contributed modestly to growth for the first time since late 2024.

Household demand carried into June. Inflation-adjusted consumer spending rose 0.4%, matching its strongest increase since July 2025, with spending supported by durable goods, recreation, restaurants and accommodation. The saving rate nevertheless fell to its lowest since 2022, while July’s renewed increase in gasoline prices threatened to erode the support previously supplied by tax refunds and promotions.

Inflation data were more favorable but did not erase the policy tension. The PCE price index fell 0.1% in June and its 3.7% annual increase matched economists’ expectations after 4.1% in May. The measure excluding food and energy rose less than forecast. The improvement occurred during a month in which an earlier pause in U.S.-Iran hostilities had reduced energy costs, making its durability uncertain after fighting resumed.

Weekly jobless claims remained low, adding a separate indication that the labor market had not weakened enough to force the Fed away from its inflation objective. The combination of softer monthly prices, firm employment and 3.9% private domestic demand gave officials evidence for both patience and eventual tightening. It did not provide the clear deterioration in either inflation or activity that could anchor the timing of the next move.

Interest-rate markets consequently restored some probability of a September increase after eliminating the risk of immediate action in July. Swaps implied about a two-in-three chance of a quarter-point increase at the September meeting, below the fully priced move before the Fed held rates at 3.5% to 3.75%. The implied probability of a second increase by year-end fell to about 40%.

The clearing of the July decision also triggered a large positioning unwind. Open interest in the August federal-funds futures contract dropped by roughly 140,000 contracts after positions had exceeded 1 million futures, representing about $5 trillion of notional exposure. The contract, which expires before the September meeting, had become the principal vehicle for hedging an immediate rate increase. Its rapid rally after the hold forced short positions to be closed or reduced.

That adjustment explains the front-end decline, but it does not explain why the long end remained under pressure. Warsh had emphasized that higher market yields were already restraining the economy and could perform some of the central bank’s work. If the Fed remains on hold because market borrowing costs are high, investors have little reason to reduce those costs without clearer evidence that inflation is returning to target. The market-led tightening therefore contains a self-reinforcing element: lower long yields would remove part of the restraint cited as a reason for delaying a policy increase.

Warsh added another source of uncertainty by saying he was examining a broader set of inflation measures than PCE. He maintained the commitment to 2% inflation and said the Fed was still using PCE, but left open the possibility that task forces reviewing the policy framework and economic data could influence strategy after January. He did not identify an alternative measure.

That ambiguity matters because the choice of index affects how investors interpret both the goal and the path toward it. Former Richmond Fed President Jeffrey Lacker said the PCE and consumer price indexes were the only broad, reliable candidates. JPMorgan economist Michael Feroli warned that changing the framework could appear to redefine the inflation problem rather than solve it, while Barclays strategist Jon Hill linked reduced confidence in the Fed’s commitment to greater term and inflation risk premiums.

Thursday’s 1-basis-point decline in the 10-year breakeven showed that the concern did not intensify continuously through the session. It remained significant because the initial post-meeting rise was concentrated farther along the curve, where a change in the policy framework would have the greatest cumulative effect. The 30-year sector was also where the largest cash-market activity increases occurred: Treasury par trading in maturities longer than 20 years rose 17.8% from Wednesday, while activity in the greater-than-10-year through 20-year sector increased 37.5%. Those figures identify the center of the repricing without indicating whether customers were net buyers or sellers.

Middle East developments kept the inflation distribution wide. The U.S. struck dozens of Iranian military targets after Tehran attacked an American base in Jordan. Drones also hit two liquefied-natural-gas tankers near Egypt’s Mediterranean coast, and Saudi Arabia and Iraq became more directly involved in the widening conflict.

Oil nevertheless fell because the American attack avoided key bridges and other civilian infrastructure and shipping through the Strait of Hormuz showed signs of recovery. Qatar sent its first LNG cargo through the strait in more than three weeks. Brent declined 1.5% to $89.38 and WTI slipped 0.56% to $83.99, although they remained 22.19% and 18.71% higher over a month, respectively. The daily fall restrained breakevens, but the cumulative increase and continuing attacks prevented the energy shock from becoming yesterday’s problem.

## The BOE Relieves Gilts as Japan Defends the Yen

The Bank of England produced a clearer front-end rally by separating current domestic disinflation from the conditional threat posed by energy. The Monetary Policy Committee voted 6-3 to keep the bank rate at 3.75%. Catherine Mann joined Megan Greene and Chief Economist Huw Pill in favoring a quarter-point increase, but Governor Andrew Bailey and the other five members saw enough easing in domestic price pressure to wait.

Bailey explicitly rejected the idea that the committee was moving closer to a rate increase. Deputy Governor Clare Lombardelli, often viewed as one of the more hawkish officials, said her decision to hold had not been close. Policymakers cited clear signs of softer domestic inflation pressure and little evidence that higher energy costs had yet spread into wages and broader prices.

Traders reduced the probability of a September increase to about 35% and priced roughly 32 basis points of tightening by year-end, down from 42 basis points on Wednesday. The 2-year gilt yield fell 11 basis points to 4.34%, its largest decline since June 12. The 10-year yield dropped 4 basis points to 4.99%, while the 30-year was little changed at 5.73%, producing a steepening that resembled the U.S. pattern but arose from more direct resistance to near-term tightening.

The vote revealed a widening division over how to handle the energy shock. Pill argued that an increase would cut through commodity-market noise, Mann emphasized policy credibility and Greene judged that an early move could reduce the probability of second-round effects. On the other side, Deputy Governor Dave Ramsden and external member Alan Taylor said they could consider resuming rate cuts if the conflict ended quickly and domestic disinflation continued.

The BOE’s central forecast put inflation at 3.2% at the end of 2026, up from 2.6% currently, before returning toward 2% next year. That path assumed the stop-start character of the Middle East conflict continued. In an adverse scenario, with oil above $100 and gas prices 60% higher, inflation reached 4.5% in Q2 2027. A milder outcome involving quicker de-escalation produced a 3% peak and fewer second-round effects. GDP growth remained around 1% in 2026 and 2027 across the scenarios.

Balance-sheet policy preserved pressure farther along the gilt curve. The BOE estimated that quantitative tightening had added 20 to 30 basis points to 10-year yields, about 5 basis points more than its estimate a year earlier. It will decide the next year of the program in September. Fiscal uncertainty before the autumn budget also left long-maturity investors with less reason to follow the front-end rally.

Euro-area data supplied a different reason for caution about easing financial conditions. GDP increased 0.4% in Q2 after stagnation at the start of the year, doubling the consensus forecast and producing the strongest quarterly growth in more than a year. All four major economies expanded despite higher energy costs from the Iran war.

Germany grew 0.2%, while first-quarter growth was revised up to 0.4%. France expanded 0.2% after a 0.1% contraction, with consumer spending and trade offsetting a second consecutive decline in investment. Italy also grew 0.2%. Spain again led the group with a 0.7% increase, supported by household spending, tourism, migration and European Union funds.

The growth surprise arrived alongside firmer inflation indications. Spanish inflation accelerated to 3.8% in July, and German regional readings also rose. Euro-area inflation due Friday was expected to edge up to 2.9%. The ECB had already warned that the energy shock created upside inflation and downside growth risks; the stronger output figures reduced the evidence for the downside half of that assessment and supported expectations that another increase could come in September.

Japan faced a more immediate collision between monetary policy, sovereign yields and the currency. The yen strengthened as much as 3.3% against the dollar in New York trading, its largest intraday gain since December 2023, after Japanese authorities intervened to support it, according to a market participant and reporting by the Nikkei. U.S. authorities also requested quotes on dollar-yen, a step associated with evaluating market conditions. Treasury Secretary Scott Bessent described the yen as very undervalued and excessive volatility as unhealthy.

The yen closed at 159.53 per dollar and held most of the advance into early Asian trading. The move extended the dollar’s broader post-Fed decline and occurred immediately before the BOJ decision, increasing the prospect that intervention and monetary guidance would be assessed together. Japan had already spent a record ¥11.73 trillion supporting the currency in the prior quarter, probably drawing in part on foreign securities including Treasuries.

Domestic bonds were also signaling pressure for further normalization. A 2-year JGB auction produced a bid-to-cover ratio of 3.63, down from 4.82 at the prior sale and below the 12-month average of 3.81. The auction tail widened to 0.007 from 0.005, even though the security offered the highest yield of the year. The 2-year yield traded around 1.47%, close to the 1.52% peak reached earlier in July.

The auction was not a failed sale, but it showed that the highest yield of the year had not restored demand to its recent average. Overnight-indexed swaps assigned about a 25% probability to a BOJ increase by September and 79% by October. The weaker auction, renewed intervention and the currency’s sensitivity to the U.S.-Japan rate gap raised the importance of Governor Kazuo Ueda’s guidance even though a hold remained the expected outcome.

## AI Borrowers Clear the Market After Conceding Price and Protection

The repricing of artificial-intelligence finance moved from negotiation to completed transactions. CoreWeave locked in a $2.6 billion leveraged loan at 5.5 percentage points over the benchmark, 1 percentage point above the upper end of its initial 4.25-to-4.5-point range. The loan was offered at 96 to 97 cents on the dollar and was expected to yield more than 9%.

The concessions drew about $9 billion of orders. That demand allowed the transaction to close, but at an estimated additional annual interest cost of about $30 million relative to the original upper end of the marketed margin. Spreads on a euro-denominated CoreWeave bond touched 1,000 basis points during Thursday’s trading, and some corporate bonds had recently fallen below 90 cents for yields in the low teens before recovering with the broader technology rally.

The loan finances chips and other computing equipment for take-or-pay contracts involving Anthropic, Jane Street and Hudson River Trading. It can be drawn over time, so interest is paid only on borrowed amounts, and its principal amortizes to zero over its life. Moody’s assigned a Ba2 rating and Fitch rated it BB+, at the higher end of speculative grade.

The structure did not eliminate the principal mismatch. The weighted average life of the underlying client contracts was about 3.1 years, shorter than the loan’s 5-year maturity. The customer agreements represented roughly $4 billion of initially contracted revenue, and CoreWeave guaranteed cash-flow shortfalls while a replacement tenant was found. Lenders were nevertheless taking renewal and residual demand risk that had not been present to the same degree in the company’s earlier broadly syndicated chip-backed financing.

That distinction helps explain why the $9 billion orderbook coexisted with much higher pricing. Investors were willing to fund identifiable contracts and collateral, but required compensation for the possibility that the leases ended before the debt. The transaction also arrived as CoreWeave prepared to spend more than $34 billion this year and as repeated data-center deals competed for the same pool of capital.

Proofpoint’s $5 billion refinancing also cleared only after lenders changed the bargain. The Thoma Bravo-owned cybersecurity company extended $4.3 billion of loans by two years, while $735 million remains due in 2028. The extended portion priced at 4.5 percentage points above the benchmark, compared with a 3-point margin on the existing financing.

The company altered roughly two dozen provisions. An omni blocker restricts transactions that could move collateral beyond existing lenders’ reach, while another provision prohibits privately negotiated debt repurchases that favor selected creditors. Orders had been sufficient to approve the transaction before the original deadline, but some investors submitted commitments on the expectation that those protections would be added, prompting an extension of the process.

Proofpoint and CoreWeave therefore completed different forms of technology financing through the same broad adjustment in creditor power. CoreWeave paid more for contract-backed growth capital whose leases expire before the debt. Proofpoint paid more and surrendered document flexibility to refinance a mature software capital structure exposed to AI disruption. Completion demonstrated access to capital, while the price and protections showed the conditions attached to that access.

Investment-grade borrowers were encountering the same supply constraint at lower spreads. Equinix began marketing at least $3 billion of bonds in as many as four tranches from 3 to 10 years, with initial guidance on the longest maturity around 140 basis points over Treasuries. The data-center company’s capital spending rose 60% from a year earlier to $1.58 billion in Q2. Proceeds were intended for property and business acquisitions, development projects and debt repayment.

The transaction placed another large AI-related financing into a market already absorbing repeated loans, project bonds and corporate issuance. Unlike CoreWeave, Equinix entered with investment-grade access and a diversified data-center portfolio. Its announced size and use of proceeds still made the final pricing important for determining whether the increase in financing costs remained concentrated among leveraged borrowers or was spreading through the infrastructure sector.

Banks were also transferring part of their exposure to the buildout. Société Générale was finalizing a significant-risk-transfer transaction covering about $5 billion of project-finance loans across energy, renewable power and data centers. Such deals typically provide protection on 5% to 15% of the referenced portfolio, freeing regulatory capital while giving investors coupons that can exceed 10%.

SRT issuance exceeded $18 billion in the first half of 2026, compared with about $15 billion a year earlier, and was on course for a sixth consecutive annual record. SocGen had recently transferred risk on more than €9 billion of corporate loans in a separate transaction priced at 675 basis points over a benchmark. The growth of the market showed that banks could continue originating infrastructure loans while distributing a concentrated first-loss exposure to specialist investors.

Demand was also migrating toward shorter corporate maturities. Bonds due in less than 5 years outperformed the broader euro investment-grade index over the prior month, and U.S. credit showed a similar pattern. Debt maturing in less than 1 year was close to flat over that period, compared with a 0.9% decline in the broad index and a loss of more than 2.9% for maturities of at least 10 years. The yield pickup from 3-year to 9-year bonds was only 67 basis points, limiting the compensation for assuming substantially more interest-rate exposure.

The preference was consistent with the Treasury curve and the primary-market concessions. Investors could preserve income at short and intermediate maturities without taking the full effect of rising term premiums. Longer corporate debt remained exposed to both Treasury duration and the possibility that heavy technology issuance would require additional spread.

## Private-Credit Defaults Rise as Long-Dollar Funding Gets Harder

Stress was more advanced in private credit. Fitch Ratings’ trailing 12-month default rate across 1,300 U.S. private-debt borrowers rose to a record 6% at the end of Q2, from the previous high of 5.7% in Q1. The agency recorded 32 default events involving 20 new borrowers during the quarter, bringing the number of defaulters to 84.

Maturity extensions under stress overtook payment-in-kind arrangements and interest deferrals as the leading source of quarterly defaults. More than half of the 32 events involved an extension, showing that borrowers were increasingly unable to refinance on original schedules even when lenders avoided a conventional payment failure.

Industrials and manufacturing recorded the highest sector default rate at 10.4%, up from 5.9% in Q1. Healthcare rose to 9.4% from 6.9%. Software moved in the opposite direction, with its default rate falling to 1.2% from 2.3%, despite investor concern that AI could weaken established technology businesses. Fitch expected defaults to remain elevated because rate cuts had not arrived and merger activity remained subdued.

Xerox demonstrated one way a stressed borrower was raising liquidity before its maturities. The company recognized $105 million of tariff-refund receivables in Q2 and sold the claim to a third party for $80 million in cash. It used a meaningful portion of the proceeds to repurchase debt below face value.

The company carried $4.2 billion of total debt, including $556 million of unsecured notes due in August 2028 that traded around 60 cents on the dollar. Revenue increased 22% from a year earlier to $1.9 billion following the acquisition of Lexmark, but declined 7% on a pro-forma basis. Xerox raised its full-year revenue forecast to $7.6 billion, while management identified maturities in 2028, 2029 and 2030 as the central balance-sheet challenge.

The sale converted a legally contingent refund claim into immediate cash at a 24% discount to its recognized value. It also allowed Xerox to retire debt at a discount, potentially capturing part of the gap between the cash purchase price of the claim and the depressed market value of its obligations. The transaction improved near-term flexibility without changing the scale of the refinancing still required.

Long-dollar funding was also becoming harder for Asian borrowers. Indonesia’s Danantara delayed progress on a planned sale of 20- and 30-year dollar bonds after investors sought more yield than the sovereign wealth fund was prepared to pay. The rise in long Treasury yields magnified the problem because the contemplated maturities were particularly sensitive to changes in the underlying risk-free curve.

The resignation of Bank Indonesia Governor Perry Warjiyo added an issuer-specific premium. Danantara, which controls assets valued by officials at about $900 billion, is little more than a year old and continues to face questions about governance, transparency and its connection to President Prabowo Subianto’s state-led economic program. The rupiah was down nearly 8% against the dollar for the year, and the fund’s planned sale would have followed a $1.5 billion international bond debut in June.

Other emerging-market borrowers were looking beyond dollars. Kenya was considering its first yuan-denominated bond in China’s domestic market, potentially raising the equivalent of $300 million by year-end to help finance its fiscal deficit through June 2027. Yuan sovereign and corporate bonds issued during the year yielded about 2.17% on average, less than half the rate on emerging-market dollar debt.

The plans remained preliminary, and size and timing could change. Kenya expected its fiscal deficit to narrow to 5.5% of GDP from 6.7% in the previous year, while high debt service, government arrears and weak tax collection continued to constrain its finances. More than half its external debt was denominated in dollars, compared with 12% in yuan, giving a panda bond both a funding-cost rationale and a currency-diversification role.

Malaysia showed the opposite side of Asian local-currency flows. Foreign investors sold a net $1.4 billion of Malaysian bonds in July, the largest outflow since October 2024. The 10-year yield rose about 10 basis points during the month as some investors brought forward expectations of a rate increase after GDP grew 5.8% from a year earlier in Q2.

The outflow occurred despite contained inflation of 1.9%, an investment-grade sovereign profile and a domestic investor base that had kept Malaysian debt more resilient than several regional peers during the Iran war. Most surveyed economists expected Bank Negara Malaysia to retain its 2.75% policy rate through at least 2027. The combination left the market exposed to short-term foreign repositioning without establishing a lasting deterioration in the country’s fiscal or inflation fundamentals.

## Forward Market Significance

The Bank of Japan’s July 31 decision is the immediate policy test. All 52 surveyed economists expected the benchmark rate to remain at 1% after June’s increase, shifting attention to updated forecasts, Ueda’s press conference and any discussion of the currency. A hold accompanied by guidance that preserves a possible move by October would align with current swap pricing; a message that pushes tightening farther away would leave intervention carrying more of the burden of defending the yen.

The interaction with Japanese government bonds is as important as the policy rate. The 2-year auction’s 3.63 bid-to-cover ratio and wider tail showed weaker demand even at the highest yield of the year. Earlier guidance about another increase could support the yen but place additional pressure on short JGBs, while a longer delay could renew the rate-gap trade that helped drive the currency to a four-decade low.

Friday’s euro-area inflation release will determine whether the stronger Q2 growth result is accompanied by a broader acceleration in prices. A reading near the expected 2.9%, after Spanish inflation rose to 3.8% and German regional measures accelerated, would keep a September ECB increase under consideration. A softer result would give greater weight to the central bank’s concern that the energy shock may weaken growth before it creates sustained second-round inflation.

For the Fed, the next inflation and employment readings must do more than change the probability of a September move. They must clarify whether Warsh’s broader inflation lens alters the threshold for action. Softer data could reinforce the front-end rally, but the long end may remain resistant if the Fed continues to cite high market yields as a substitute for tightening. Persistent inflation would make the three July dissenters look more prescient and increase pressure for policy action that validates the steepening already imposed by investors.

The Treasury’s announcement of auction sizes for the August-to-October quarter adds a separate duration test. Sizes were expected to remain steady, but investors will assess whether the financing guidance prepares the market for increases next year. With the 30-year yield above 5.2%, even a deferred change in supply can affect the term premium if it brings larger long-maturity borrowing closer.

The Middle East conflict remains capable of changing both policy distributions before those releases arrive. Qatar’s return to Hormuz and Thursday’s decline in crude limited the immediate inflation response to fresh U.S. strikes. Further attacks on tankers, Egyptian waters or Gulf infrastructure would challenge that relief, while sustained shipping could reduce the energy premium even without a full political settlement.

AI financing will be judged through execution rather than announced demand alone. CoreWeave attracted $9 billion of orders, but only after locking in a 550-basis-point margin and accepting refinancing risk around contracts shorter than the loan. Proofpoint extended most of its debt after paying a higher margin and adding creditor protections. Equinix’s multi-tranche bond sale will show how much of that repricing reaches an investment-grade data-center issuer with a broader business and shorter maturities.

The final distinction is between available capital and inexpensive capital. Corporate loans, bonds, SRTs, panda bonds and distressed claim sales all remained usable sources of funding. Their terms increasingly reflected the same pressures visible in the Treasury curve: high real yields, uncertainty about inflation, heavy technology investment and less confidence that central banks will anchor long borrowing costs through clear guidance.

section_summaries.summary: The BOE voted 6-3 to hold at 3.75% and rejected the idea that an increase was drawing closer, sending the 2-year gilt yield down 11 basis points while long gilts lagged. Stronger euro-area growth and firmer inflation readings preserved the case for a September ECB increase. In Japan, yen intervention and weaker demand at a 2-year JGB auction increased the importance of Ueda’s guidance ahead of the BOJ decision.

section_summaries.market_read: Demand shifted toward shorter maturities, where investors could retain income with less Treasury-duration exposure.
section_summaries.next_check: Equinix’s final pricing will show how far higher financing costs have spread into investment-grade AI infrastructure.
section_summaries.section_title: AI Borrowers Clear the Market After Conceding Price and Protection
section_summaries.summary: CoreWeave secured its $2.6 billion loan only after raising the margin to 5.5 percentage points and leaving lenders exposed to contracts shorter than the 5-year debt. Proofpoint extended $4.3 billion of loans after paying a higher margin and adding creditor protections. Equinix’s planned bond sale and growing bank risk transfers showed that AI-related capital remained available, but investors increasingly demanded compensation, safeguards or shorter maturities.

section_summaries.market_read: Extensions overtaking PIK and interest deferrals showed that refinancing stress increasingly drove private-credit defaults.
section_summaries.section_title: Private-Credit Defaults Rise as Long-Dollar Funding Gets Harder
section_summaries.summary: The U.S. private-credit default rate reached a record 6% in Q2 as stressed maturity extensions became the leading form of default. Xerox raised cash by selling a tariff-refund claim at a discount before repurchasing debt below face value. Higher long Treasury yields and issuer concerns delayed Danantara’s planned dollar bonds, while Kenya considered yuan funding and foreign investors withdrew from Malaysian bonds.

section_summaries.market_read: Capital remained available across public and private markets, but its price and protections increasingly reflected high real yields and policy uncertainty.
section_summaries.summary: The BOJ decision and Ueda’s guidance will test whether intervention can be paired with a credible path toward another increase. Euro-area inflation will determine whether stronger growth keeps a September ECB move in play, while incoming U.S. inflation and employment data must clarify the Fed’s threshold for action. Treasury supply guidance, Middle East shipping and Equinix’s pricing remain separate tests of duration risk, energy inflation and financing conditions.

overall_summary.headline: Treasury curve steepens as Fed uncertainty keeps pressure on the long end
overall_summary.session_narrative:
At the July 30 close, Treasury yields fell 2.7 basis points to 4.247% at 2 years and 0.5 basis point to 4.674% at 10 years, while the 30-year rose 1.2 basis points to 5.215%. The 2s30s curve widened 3.9 basis points to 96.8 basis points, and the 30-year had touched about 5.24%, a fresh 19-year high. The move extended the post-Fed steepening: the July hold and a large federal-funds futures unwind supported the front end, but investors still demanded compensation for inflation and an unclear reaction function at longer maturities.

Q2 GDP slowed to 1.5%, yet consumer spending grew 3.2% and private domestic demand 3.9%, while weekly claims stayed low. June PCE fell 0.1% on the month and eased to 3.7% annually, but renewed Middle East fighting clouded the durability of the earlier energy relief. The 10-year real yield rose 0.5 basis point as the breakeven declined 1 basis point, showing stabilization rather than a full reversal of the initial inflation-risk repricing. A sharp technology rebound, weaker dollar and firmer gold did not pull long Treasuries into the relief move.

The BOE’s 6-3 hold produced an 11-basis-point drop in the 2-year gilt yield, while yen intervention and a weaker 2-year JGB auction raised the stakes for the July 31 BOJ decision. Technology financing remained available on tougher terms: CoreWeave paid a 550-basis-point margin, and Proofpoint paid more while adding creditor protections. Private-credit defaults reached a record 6%, with maturity extensions becoming the leading form of default.
overall_summary.summary: Front-end Treasury yields eased after the Fed held rates, but the 30-year yield rose and the curve steepened as resilient domestic demand, still-high inflation and unclear guidance kept term-premium pressure concentrated at the long end.
